text:
Alana: Quick q — for these new large-vocab models (200k+ tokens), we can't afford the full bench for every PR. How should we prioritize validation so we catch regressions but keep cost down?

kevin: +1 on needing a tiered approach. My quick take: stratified sampling across token-length buckets and rare-token density. Run a tiny perf microbench (3 seeds) + functional smoke + small gold-set eval. That covers most surprises.

sara: We do something similar on infra for large images. Suggest explicit acceptance tiers:
- Tier 0 (sanity): model loads, forward pass w/ tiny batch
- Tier 1 (behavioral): 50 golden prompts for hallucination/formatting checks
- Tier 2 (compat/perf): compact bench sampling (~5% of bench) focused on worst-case seq lengths and kv-cache churn
- Tier 3 (full): full bench gated to on-call or nightly schedule (cost charged to team)

kevin: For large-vocab models, rare-token stress tests should be prioritized in Tier 2. They surface tokenizer-induced OOMs and latency spikes. Also measure avg top-k token probability mass shift vs baseline (simple metric).

Alana: Nice. How do we pick the 5% bench subset for Tier 2? random vs targeted?

sara: Targeted. heuristic: pick examples by:
- highest token-length percentile (95th+)
- top percentiles of new-token-rate (how many tokens are OOV/new compared to our catalog)
- samples that force kv-cache eviction patterns (long context + repeated prefixes)

kevin: Here's a small gating config prototype that the onboarding harness could use (pseudo-yaml):
```
gating:
  tier0: { timeout: 30s, checks: [load, forward] }
  tier1: { gold_prompts: 50, fail_if_hallucination_rate > 0.15 }
  tier2: { perf_samples: 100, focus: [long_seq, rare_token], max_latency_p50_ms: 120 }
  tier3: { run_full_bench: true, schedule: nightly }
```

Alana: I like explicit thresholds. We should also capture a policy for graceful-degrade routing when Tier 2 misses perf SLOs (e.g., route to quantized variant or fall back to smaller model).

sara: +1. Also add an economic gate: if run cost for a model exceeds multiplier X of baseline, require approval from cost owner before full bench. That prevents surprise bills.

ops-bot: note: can add auto-labels on registry entries: "large-vocab" and "cost-flag". Those trigger different CI queues.

kevin: One more tradeoff: coverage vs speed. To detect semantic regressions we need diverse prompts, but that grows eval cost. Proposal: keep an evolving small gold set per vertical + augment with synthetic perturbations to increase coverage cheaply.

Alana: OK actionable items:
- kevin: sketch the Tier2 sample selector and metric list (PR by Thu)
- sara: add cost-approval flow and the draft gating yaml into onboarding repo (PR by Fri)
- ops-bot: add auto-label + CI-queue mapping (ticket created)

sara: I'll also prototype a small dashboard that shows Tier pass rates + per-model rare-token penalty so product teams can prioritize fixes.

Alana: Thanks — will sync in tomorrow's onboarding sync. @kevin @sara :thumbsup:
